The pipeline adds $\sim$6.4\% overhead; net acceleration requires kernel-level sparse computation optimizations (e.g., Triton block-sparse, cuSPARSE) that are beyond the scope of this work.

5	\paragraph{Model and Predictor.}
6	We evaluate on LLaMA-3.1-8B~\cite{grattafiori2024llama3}, which uses SwiGLU FFN blocks~\cite{shazeer2020glu} with $d_{\text{model}}=4096$ and $d_{\text{ff}}=14336$ across 32 layers.
7	The sparsity predictor is a two-layer MLP with 2.37M parameters per layer (75.9M total), implemented as Linear($4096 \to 128$) + GELU + Linear($128 \to 14336$), trained to produce per-neuron importance scores that minimize output-distribution divergence under sparsity.
8	
9	\paragraph{Training.}
10	All predictors are trained for 1000 steps on WikiText-103 with sequence length 2048 and batch size 4 on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU (96\,GB), using AdamW~\cite{loshchilov2019adamw} with learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, weight decay $1 \times 10^{-2}$, and cosine decay.

12

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Our experiments demonstrate that \emph{coupling alignment}---optimizing a composable, output-level quantity---is necessary for sparsity prediction quality, a principle well-established in end-to-end learning but previously unverified for activation sparsity.
A target-swap ablation confirms that KL-discovered mask patterns (46--68\% divergent from magnitude) drive inference-stage quality; gradient coupling is necessary for mask discovery but not at inference.
A predictor ($<$1\% of base) reduces TEAL's perplexity by 14.5\% at matched sparsity and renders compensation networks redundant.
However, PPL gains do not uniformly transfer: KL improves commonsense reasoning (4/4 tasks) but underperforms on knowledge-intensive benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K); preliminary cross-architecture evaluation (Mistral-7B: 5/6 tasks) and scale analysis (14B: reasoning declines despite PPL gains) reveal task- and scale-dependent effects.
Future work includes N:M structured sparsity and scaling to 70B+.
